1.explanation: The TableHeader function component is the key bug-related element because it directly manages the rendering of table header cells (<th>) and the distribution of props via ...rest. The bug is caused by ...rest being spread onto the <button> element for sortable headers instead of the <th>, preventing props like id from being set on the correct element. Thus, any fix requires modifying the TableHeader component/function to ensure ...rest is always applied to the <th>, regardless of whether the column is sortable. No other classes or functions are involved based on the provided compressed bug files and context.
1.bug_scenario: The bug involves the TableHeader component from carbon-components-react, where additional props (spread with ...rest) are passed to the wrong element for sortable table headers. For non-sortable headers, ...rest is passed to the <th> element, allowing for custom props like id to be set for accessibility (A11y) and other purposes. However, for sortable headers, ...rest is passed to the inner <button> instead of the <th>. This means important props like id do not reach the <th> element when the column is sortable, breaking accessibility requirements (such as WCAG H43) and causing inconsistent behavior.

2.explanation: The bug is specifically related to the TableHeader functional component, which both defines and uses the ...rest props pattern. The core logic for applying props to either the <th> or <button> elements is entirely contained within the TableHeader function. The misplacement of ...rest in the render logic for sortable headers (applying it to <button> instead of <th>) directly causes the accessibility issue. There are no other relevant classes or functions in the compressed file; the TableHeader function is the singular focus for this bug.
2.bug_scenario: The bug arises in the TableHeader component of carbon-components-react, where extra props (such as id for accessibility purposes) passed via ...rest are only applied to the <th> element for non-sortable headers. For sortable headers, ...rest is incorrectly applied to the inner <button> instead of the <th>. This causes issues such as id attributes not being set at the correct place for sortable headers, which can break accessibility and referencing, as shown in the WCAG violation described in the bug report.
